house-viewing.title: Viewing an Apartment
house-viewing.subtitle: Ask about rent, bills, and the lease.
house-viewing.culture: Rent in Chinese cities is usually paid monthly or every few months, often with a deposit of one or two months. Many apartments are rented through agents who charge a fee, and water, electricity, and internet are usually billed separately.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ xiǎng kàn fángzi.
dialogue.en: Hello, I would like to see an apartment.

words.en: to look / to watch / to read

dialogue.speaker: agent
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ yào zhǎo shénmeyàng de?
dialogue.en: What kind are you looking for?

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Yī gè dānjiān, duōshǎo qián?
dialogue.en: How much is a single room?

dialogue.speaker: agent
dialogue.text: 一个月三千五，水电另算。
dialogue.pinyin: Yī gè yuè sānqiān wǔ, shuǐdiàn lìngsuàn.
dialogue.en: Three thousand five hundred yuan per month, utilities not included.

choices.en: Is internet included in the rent?
Can I rent it for a short period?
Is it far from the subway?

utilities-bill.title: Paying Utility Bills
utilities-bill.subtitle: Pay water, electricity, and gas bills.
utilities-bill.culture: Most utility bills in China can be paid through WeChat or Alipay, or at convenience stores. You usually need your account number, and many landlords handle these bills directly.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ yào jiāo shuǐdiànfèi.
dialogue.en: Hello, I need to pay my utility bill.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ de hùhào shì duōshǎo?
dialogue.en: What is your account number?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ shǒujī shàng néng jiāo ma?
dialogue.en: Can I pay on my phone?

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.text: 可以，用微信或者支付宝。
dialogue.pinyin: Kěyǐ, yòng wēixìn huòzhě zhīfùbǎo.
dialogue.en: Yes, you can use WeChat or Alipay.

choices.en: Where do I pay the gas bill?
How much is the electricity bill for this month?
I'll pay two hundred.

home-repair.title: Reporting a Repair
home-repair.subtitle: Ask someone to fix a pipe or the air conditioner.
home-repair.culture: Most apartment buildings have a property management office (物业) that handles repairs. Small issues like a leaking pipe or a broken AC are often fixed for free, though you may pay for parts.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒjiā shuǐguǎn lòushuǐ le.
dialogue.en: Hello, my water pipe is leaking.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Shì shuǐguǎn háishì kōngtiáo?
dialogue.en: Is it the water pipe or the air conditioner?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 水管坏了，能找人来修吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Shuǐguǎn huàile, néng zhǎo rén lái xiū ma?
dialogue.en: The water pipe is broken. Can I get someone to fix it?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, jīntiān xiàwǔ pài rén qù.
dialogue.en: Okay, I'll send someone this afternoon.

choices.en: The air conditioner isn't cooling.
When will it be fixed?
Does it cost money to fix the water pipe?

parcel-delivery.title: Picking Up a Package
parcel-delivery.subtitle: Collect a delivery at the pickup station.
parcel-delivery.culture: In China, packages are often delivered to a pickup station or locker (菜鸟驿站) rather than your door. You get a pickup code (取件码) by text, and you use it to collect your parcel.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ qǔ kuàidì.
dialogue.en: Hello, I'm here to pick up my package.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Bào yīxià qǔjiànmǎ.
dialogue.en: Can you give me the pickup code?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Qǔjiànmǎ shì liùsānwǔ.
dialogue.en: The pickup code is 635.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Shì zhège bāoguǒ ma?
dialogue.en: Is this the package?

choices.en: Has my delivery arrived?
Can I leave it at the door?

words.en: to put / to place / to release

choices.en: I didn't receive the pickup code.

laundry.title: At the Laundry Shop
laundry.subtitle: Drop off clothes and ask when to collect.
laundry.culture: Dry cleaners (洗衣店) in China offer washing and dry cleaning, and many also iron clothes. Next-day service is common, and the price depends on the item.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, zhè jiàn yīfú yào xǐ.
dialogue.en: Hello, I need to wash this garment.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Shuǐxǐ háishì gānxǐ?
dialogue.en: Should it be washed or dry-cleaned?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Shuǐxǐ ba, shénme shíhòu néng qǔ?
dialogue.en: Let's wash it. When can I pick it up?

words.en: particle indicating suggestion or softening tone

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Hòutiān jiù néng qǔ.
dialogue.en: You can pick it up the day after tomorrow.

choices.pinyin: Xǐ yī jiàn dàyī duōshǎo qián?
choices.en: How much is it to wash a coat?
Can you iron this?
Can you wash it a bit faster?

hairdresser.title: At the Hairdresser
hairdresser.subtitle: Ask for a haircut and say how short.
hairdresser.culture: A basic haircut in China is usually cheap, around 30 to 80 yuan. Many salons ask whether you want a wash and blow-dry included, and tipping is not expected.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ jiǎn tóufǎ.
dialogue.en: Hello, I’d like to get a haircut.

dialogue.speaker: barber
dialogue.pinyin: Jiǎn duō duǎn?
dialogue.en: How short should I cut it?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Jiǎn duǎn yīdiǎnr, bùyào tài duǎn.
dialogue.en: Cut it a bit shorter, but not too short.

dialogue.speaker: barber
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de.
dialogue.en: Okay.

choices.en: How much is it to wash hair?
I just want to trim my bangs.
I’d like to dye my hair.

noise-complaint.title: Complaining About Noise
noise-complaint.subtitle: Ask property management to stop loud neighbors.
noise-complaint.culture: If neighbors are noisy, you can talk to them directly or ask the property management (物业) to step in. Chinese apartments are close together, so keeping noise down after 10 p.m. is expected.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, lóu shàng tài chǎo le.
dialogue.en: Hello, it’s too noisy upstairs.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Jǐ diǎn kāishǐ de?
dialogue.en: What time did it start?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Wǎnshàng shíyī diǎn hái zài chǎo.
dialogue.en: It’s still noisy at 11 PM.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, wǒmen qù shuō yīxià.
dialogue.en: Okay, we’ll go talk to them.

choices.en: They’ve been noisy the whole time.
I need to sleep tonight.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

choices.pinyin: Néng bāng wǒ gōutōng yīxià ma?
choices.en: Could you help me communicate?

send-parcel.title: Sending a Parcel
send-parcel.subtitle: Mail a package and ask the price.
send-parcel.culture: Express delivery (快递) in China is fast and cheap; most packages arrive the next day or within two days. Companies like SF Express (顺丰) offer same-city or next-day service.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ yào jì gè bāoguǒ.
dialogue.en: Hello, I want to send a package.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.pinyin: Jì dào nǎlǐ?
dialogue.en: Where should I send it to?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Jì dào shànghǎi, duōshǎo qián?
dialogue.en: How much is it to send to Shanghai?

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.pinyin: Kàn zhòngliàng, èrshí kuài zuǒyòu.
dialogue.en: It depends on the weight, around twenty yuan.

words.en: to look / to watch / to read

choices.en: Can it arrive today?
Can I insure it?
I need to send a document.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

community-gate.title: At the Community Gate
community-gate.subtitle: Talk to the guard about entry and the key card.
community-gate.culture: Most residential compounds (小区) in China have a security guard and require a key card to enter. Visitors usually register at the gate, and guards often know the residents.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ shì zhè dòng de zhùhù.
dialogue.en: Hello, I live in this building.

dialogue.speaker: guard
dialogue.pinyin: Qǐng shuā ménjìnkǎ.
dialogue.en: Please swipe your access card.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 我忘带卡了，能帮我开一下吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ wàng dài kǎ le, néng bāng wǒ kāi yīxià ma?
dialogue.en: I forgot my card. Can you let me in?

words.en: to open / to turn on / to write out

dialogue.speaker: guard
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, xià cì jìde dài.
dialogue.en: Okay, remember to bring it next time.

words.en: to bring / to have with you

choices.en: How do visitors register?
Where can I get a door access card?
Can delivery people enter the community?

internet-install.title: Setting Up Broadband
internet-install.subtitle: Order home internet and ask about the price.
internet-install.culture: China's main broadband providers are China Telecom, China Unicom, and China Mobile. Installation usually takes a few days, and signing a one-year contract is cheaper than paying monthly.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ xiǎng zhuāng kuāndài.
dialogue.en: Hello, I would like to install broadband.

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ yào duōshǎo zhào de?
dialogue.en: How many megabytes do you want?

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 一百兆的，一个月多少钱？
dialogue.pinyin: Yībǎizhào de, yī gè yuè duōshǎo qián?
dialogue.en: How much is 100 megabytes per month?

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.pinyin: Yī gè yuè bāshí, bāo nián piányi.
dialogue.en: It's eighty yuan per month, but it's cheaper if you pay for the year.

choices.en: When will it be installed?
Can I pay by the month?
Does the internet fee include the router?
